title: Add dissector for DECT NWK layer
description: Adds a dissector for the DECT NWK layer defined in EN 300 175-5. It is based on the skeleton mentioned in #15742 and fixes this request when finished.

can you look/fix this warning

`Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-dect-nwk.c:1560 proto_tree_add_item called for hf_dect_nwk_s_ie_auth_type_default_cipher_key_algorithm  -  item type is FT_UINT8 but call has len 2`

and from Clang (Analyzer)

`packet-dect-nwk.c:2292:6: warning: no previous prototype for function 'proto_register_dect_nwk' [-Wmissing-prototypes]
packet-dect-nwk.c:3239:6: warning: no previous prototype for function 'proto_reg_handoff_dect_nwk' [-Wmissing-prototypes]
packet-dect-nwk.c:1757:4: warning: Value stored to 'no_of_bits' is never read [deadcode.DeadStores]
packet-dect-nwk.c:1762:4: warning: Value stored to 'no_of_bits' is never read [deadcode.DeadStores]
`

can you also add dissector to docs/release-note ?

Should be fixed now. The first was most likely a copy paste error, the no_of_bits non-usage was due to a not yet implemented field dissection, that has been added.

I also added a line to the release not, I'm not sure whether I should also refer to the ETSI EN standard number there though.
typo Unkown -> Unknown (see also after)

3. FT_STRING is a bit more complicated. I'm using this field type to decode the string values. Basically I could think of assuming string values will always end on byte (or 1/2byte boundary if BCD) and use the according add_tree_item function instead of bitfield here (cross-checking the number of bits) or add FT_BYTES processing to \_proto_tree_add_bits_ret_val however in the latter case I'm not sure how to handle a byte vs number of bit mismatch. If you really expect them to be multiples of 8 (or 4 bits), maybe just should them as FT_STRING items for the number of bytes they are.  I don't really have any experience of dissecting BCD, but a quick grep in epan/dissectors shows that ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9 is usually used with proto_tree_add_item() (with an FT_STRING field). would value 0 be okej to initialize with?

Yes initialization with 0 is fine in that case. Theoretically you could even use any value as it will always be overwritten in Octet #D before it is read again in Octet #E (basically there is a 14 bit value split over two consecutive octets where the MSB in every octet identifies whether there is a following octet.) That's also the reason why I didn't explicitly initialize the variable.
Should I add the initialization or will you do it by your own?

The reason to initialise 'store_display_characters' it is that there is no real guarantee that we'll see OCTET_D before we see OCTET_E.

If it would be surprising to see E without D first, this could be reported using expert info?
Also, what if octet_identifier isn't one of the cases you have in the switch?  Would that be an error, or is it valid to just read 'octet_group_extension' following an unknown switch value?

Hm, I do not see why there would be any chance to see E without seeing D first. The DECT_NWK_S_IE_OCTET_.. enum is just a more convenient way for 0,...,9 to make it easier to read the code next to the DECT standard. As octet_identifier is only incremented by one (line 2310), exception the jump from 0 to 2) there is always D(4) before E(5). However as I said I have nothing against doing an earlier initialization here to fore come compiler warnings.

Regarding reading more octets has that is ok according to the standard, implementations need to just allow for more. I'm not sure however if it is a good idea to also display further octets that are not yet standardized.

commits_data.message:
DECT-NWK: Dissect MM messages

Added value strings for all MM messages and use S-Format IE dissection
also for MM

commits_data.title: DECT-NWK: Fix CIPHER-INFO
commits_data.message:
DECT-NWK: Fix CIPHER-INFO

The value for Escaping to proprietary algorithm was wrong and the
Boolean field Y/N was registered using the wrong base, resulting in a
failed assertion during dissection

commits_data.title: DECT-NWK: Add fixed len information elements
commits_data.message:
DECT-NWK: Add fixed len information elements

Dissection of all fixed length S-Format information elements has been
added to the dect-nwk dissector

commits_data.title: DECT-NWK: Handle CALLING-PARTY-NUMBER
commits_data.message:
DECT-NWK: Handle CALLING-PARTY-NUMBER

Add begin of dissection of S-Format Calling Party Number information
element.

commits_data.title: DECT-NWK: Move IE dissection out of LCE
commits_data.message:
DECT-NWK: Move IE dissection out of LCE

Dissection of S-Format information elements has moved to an own
function that is now also used for dissecting CC messages

commits_data.title: DECT-NWK: Begin LCE-PAGE-RESPONSE dissection
commits_data.message:
DECT-NWK: Begin LCE-PAGE-RESPONSE dissection

First steps in dissection of the LCE-PAGE-RESPONSE message. Basic
dissection for S-FORMAT information elements being mandatory or
optional in this message is included.
